name: Elemental Bracers
summary: At Silverwind Refuge, the night elves face tainted waters and seek the hand behind them. Sentinel Velene Starstrike asks you to gather intact bracers from the hostile elementals, so a divining scroll can identify who summoned them.

sections.title: Tainted Waters
sections.body: Rogue water elementals now trouble Ashenvale’s sacred waters. Unlike the wild spirits that naturally inhabit the world, these creatures show signs of artificial conjuration. At Silverwind Refuge, the Sentinels see their sudden arrival as a sign that outside corruption is reaching deeper into the forest’s waterways.

sections.title: Divining the Conjurer
sections.body: Sentinel Velene Starstrike believes someone deliberately bound and unleashed the elementals. She gives you a magical divining scroll to help identify the culprit. The spell needs a reagent tied to the summoned beings: intact bracers taken from the spirits before they dissipate. The scroll reads the lingering arcane signature on those bindings, tracing it to whoever called the elementals into being.

sections.title: A Wizard's Meddling
sections.body: When the divining scroll is cast over the intact bracers, the arcane residue confirms Velene’s worst fears: a solitary mage is churning corrupt elementals into Ashenvale’s pools. The discovery outrages the night elf defenders. They now prepare swift retribution against the summoner threatening the woodlands’ sanctity.

faq.q: Why are there water elementals in Ashenvale?
faq.answer: The hostile water elementals are not natural inhabitants living in balance with Ashenvale. An outside spellcaster summoned them, disturbing the sacred pools and provoking the night elves.

faq.q: Who gives the quest Elemental Bracers?
aliases: where to pick up elemental bracers
faq.answer: Sentinel Velene Starstrike offers the work. She is stationed at Silverwind Refuge, on the shores of Mystral Lake in Ashenvale.

faq.q: What is the purpose of the Divining Scroll?
faq.answer: The Divining Scroll reads the magical signature left on the elementals. Cast over five intact bracers, it traces the arcane tether to the summoner who created them.

faq.q: Why do only intact bracers work for the ritual?
faq.answer: Only intact bracers retain enough stable arcane resonance for the scroll to analyze. Destroying an elemental often damages or shatters its magical bindings, leaving them unable to reveal the conjurer.

faq.q: What happens after divining the scroll?
faq.answer: After you return the Divined Scroll to Sentinel Velene Starstrike, she identifies the rogue spellcaster responsible and sends you to hunt the summoner in the follow-up, Mage Summoner.

faq.q: Why does Sentinel Velene care so much about these elementals?
aliases: why night elves care about elementals
faq.answer: Night elves revere the natural purity of Ashenvale’s forests and waters. A mortal wizard deliberately polluting and destabilizing their lakes with corrupted elementals insults their guardianship.

angles.text: As a night elf, you know Ashenvale’s natural pools are sacred ground. Arcane summoners who introduce foreign corruption affront the Kaldorei.
As a mage, you can recognize how the bindings worn by conjured elementals carry their master’s arcane signature, tracing reckless conjuration to its origin.
As an Alliance member, you strengthen your standing in central Ashenvale’s contested heartlands by aiding the Silverwind Sentinels.
